1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	Rules for AI coding agents in this repo. Humans follow them too.
4	
5	Hackathon repo, EHL Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 Oct 2026. Code freeze and Live Final Sunday
6	12:00. Working agent first, polish second.
7	
8	## Rules
9	
10	- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of adding layers,
11	  fallbacks or migrations.
12	- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirement. No speculative
13	  abstractions, configuration or indirection.
14	- Grow in layers on a product that already works. Never trade a working agent for unfinished
15	  complexity.
16	- Keep components modular and concerns separated.
17	- Read `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) before writing a helper: cost function, quote parsing, data lookup
18	  and runners exist. We wrap the kit, never patch it. Guide:
19	  https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/tree/main/starter-kit
20	- Never commit secrets. Keys live in `.env`. Never print, log or paste the arena key anywhere.
21	- All changes go through a PR against `main`, reviewed by one teammate. Branch `<firstname>/<topic>`.
22	  Agents may commit, push their branch and `gh pr create`; never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
23	- Run `uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check .` before every PR.
24	- No em-dashes in prose or copy. Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines.
25	
26	## The challenge
27	
28	We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Our agent negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's
29	supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes one term sheet per case, or walks.
30	
31	- **Score** per case: `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1. C is total cost
32	  over the horizon (price, uncovered need, payment, freight, lead time, quality, tooling, index
33	  clause, relationship charge), computed exactly by `arena_kit.total_cost`. No deal scores the
34	  alternative (0 if none). A broken must-have scores 0.
35	- **Live Final**: five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, a wave's cases in parallel. Wave
36	  score = mean case score x 100; total = sum. New suppliers; up to a third mix supplier and case
37	  types practice never shows; some cite the Sunday 08:00 data release.
38	
39	**Hard rules, breaking one can disqualify us:**
40	- No human in the loop during the final. The runner starts before 12:00 and is left alone.
41	- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
42	  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`.
43	- One key per team. No attacks on the arena or other teams (prompt-injecting bots counts).
44	- The final runs the commit we submit at 12:00. No pushes after that.
45	
46	**Hard limits:**
47	- 60 s per message per thread from the supplier's reply; three timeouts in a row end the thread.
48	- 10 messages per thread, up to 3 term sheets per message, every sheet carries every `negotiable`
49	  field.
50	- Max 3 claim checks per message, one per sentence, ID and figure in the same sentence. A wrong
51	  figure or unknown ID is `contradicted` and costs trust.
52	- 10 calls/s and 10 open sessions per key.
53	- **Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team.** Sandbox (`case:D01`,
54	  `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.
55	
56	## Where things are
57	
58	| Path | What |
59	|---|---|
60	| `docs/learnings.md` | **read first**: what we know about the arena, suppliers and data, with evidence |
61	| `docs/design.md` | the agent we are building: modules, data, policy, build order |
62	| `docs/challenge.md`, `api.md`, `submission.md` | Tacto's brief, API and cost formula, hand-in (upstream copies) |
63	| `buyer/policy.py`, `runner.py` | the price engine: per-thread policy and the loop that plays a case (`docs/design.md`, Implemented) |
64	| `buyer/economics.py`, `claims.py`, `personas.py`, `writer.py`, `llm.py` | C and term planning, claim bank, persona signals, e-mail and model paragraph |
65	| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull` |
66	| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
67	| `exports/` | Saturday probe sessions as CSV/JSONL; schema in `exports/README.md` |
68	| `analysis/explore.py` | data package exploration: profiles, persona signals, report page |
69	| `data/package/` | the data package (gitignored); Sunday also `data/release-sunday/` |
70	| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office (gitignored; Saturday's committed with `-f`) |
71	| `logs/runs/`, `logs/practice-v*.log` | our decisions per move (anchor, terms, claims, prices) and the practice run logs |
72	
73	The MCP server `arena-data` (`.mcp.json`) gives SQL, ID lookup and documents over the package.
74	
75	## Commands
76	
77	```sh
78	uv sync                                         # install (Python 3.12)
79	uv run arena data                               # data package into data/

# AGENTS.md

Rules for AI coding agents in this repo. Humans follow them too.

Hackathon repo, EHL Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 Oct 2026. Code freeze and Live Final Sunday
12:00. Working agent first, polish second.

## Rules

- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of adding layers,
  fallbacks or migrations.
- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirement. No speculative
  abstractions, configuration or indirection.
- Grow in layers on a product that already works. Never trade a working agent for unfinished
  complexity.
- Keep components modular and concerns separated.
- Read `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) before writing a helper: cost function, quote parsing, data lookup
  and runners exist. We wrap the kit, never patch it. Guide:
  https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/tree/main/starter-kit
- Never commit secrets. Keys live in `.env`. Never print, log or paste the arena key anywhere.
- All changes go through a PR against `main`, reviewed by one teammate. Branch `<firstname>/<topic>`.
  Agents may commit, push their branch and `gh pr create`; never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
- Run `uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check .` before every PR.
- No em-dashes in prose or copy. Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines.

## The challenge

We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Our agent negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's
supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes one term sheet per case, or walks.

- **Score** per case: `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1. C is total cost
  over the horizon (price, uncovered need, payment, freight, lead time, quality, tooling, index
  clause, relationship charge), computed exactly by `arena_kit.total_cost`. No deal scores the
  alternative (0 if none). A broken must-have scores 0.
- **Live Final**: five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, a wave's cases in parallel. Wave
  score = mean case score x 100; total = sum. New suppliers; up to a third mix supplier and case
  types practice never shows; some cite the Sunday 08:00 data release.

**Hard rules, breaking one can disqualify us:**
- No human in the loop during the final. The runner starts before 12:00 and is left alone.
- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`.
- One key per team. No attacks on the arena or other teams (prompt-injecting bots counts).
- The final runs the commit we submit at 12:00. No pushes after that.

**Hard limits:**
- 60 s per message per thread from the supplier's reply; three timeouts in a row end the thread.
- 10 messages per thread, up to 3 term sheets per message, every sheet carries every `negotiable`
  field.
- Max 3 claim checks per message, one per sentence, ID and figure in the same sentence. A wrong
  figure or unknown ID is `contradicted` and costs trust.
- 10 calls/s and 10 open sessions per key.
- **Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team.** Sandbox (`case:D01`,
  `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.

## Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/learnings.md` | **read first**: what we know about the arena, suppliers and data, with evidence |
| `docs/design.md` | the agent we are building: modules, data, policy, build order |
| `docs/challenge.md`, `api.md`, `submission.md` | Tacto's brief, API and cost formula, hand-in (upstream copies) |
| `buyer/policy.py`, `runner.py` | the price engine: per-thread policy and the loop that plays a case (`docs/design.md`, Implemented) |
| `buyer/economics.py`, `claims.py`, `personas.py`, `writer.py`, `llm.py` | C and term planning, claim bank, persona signals, e-mail and model paragraph |
| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull` |
| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
| `exports/` | Saturday probe sessions as CSV/JSONL; schema in `exports/README.md` |
| `analysis/explore.py` | data package exploration: profiles, persona signals, report page |
| `data/package/` | the data package (gitignored); Sunday also `data/release-sunday/` |
| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office (gitignored; Saturday's committed with `-f`) |
| `logs/runs/`, `logs/practice-v*.log` | our decisions per move (anchor, terms, claims, prices) and the practice run logs |

The MCP server `arena-data` (`.mcp.json`) gives SQL, ID lookup and documents over the package.

## Commands

```sh
uv sync                                         # install (Python 3.12)
uv run arena data                               # data package into data/
uv run arena me                                 # key works? quota left?
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                   # sandbox: free
uv run buyer play case:P01 -v                   # practice: costs 1 of the team's 200
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10   # all hosted practice cases: costs 10
uv run buyer pull --set practice                # finished sessions -> logs/sessions/
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package   # local API, scripted supplier
uv run --with pandas python analysis/explore.py # data package -> analysis/out/
```

`--agent naive` plays the kit's baseline instead of ours.

## Working on the negotiation agent

- **Code owns numbers, the model owns words.** Every binding value (sheet, accept, walk away) is
  computed or checked in code with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`; every figure in an e-mail
  comes from code next to its data ID.
- **Never accept** a sheet that breaks a must-have or costs more than the alternative. Price
  unstated fields at the supplier's standard terms (`arena_kit.docs.standard_terms`).
- **Read the supplier.** What moves it is in the data (call notes, letters, news, quote remarks,
  payment history, scorecards). Trade what is cheap for us for what it values.
- **Score every lever per case.** The same term helps in one case and hurts in the next
  (coverage, payment days, start date, index clause, contract length).
- **Generalise.** No logic keyed on case or supplier IDs; runtime knowledge from the data package
  is fine if it works for unseen suppliers.
- **Don't leak** urgency, budget, a missing alternative or the target price.
- **Every model call has a hard timeout** well under 60 s, and the move still goes out if it
  fails. Measure latency per move.

## The learning loop

1. Try on the simulator or sandbox first. Spend practice quota only on a change you expect to
   help; check `uv run arena me` before batch runs.
2. After practice: `uv run buyer pull`, read `logs/sessions/` (trace, back office, cost breakdown).
3. Find why C_deal missed C_best, change the agent, score candidate sheets offline, play again.
4. Record each finding in `docs/learnings.md` in the same PR: date, tag (`arena` / `data` /
   `rules`), finding, evidence (session, case or data ID), consequence for the agent. Untested
   ideas go under Hypotheses; correct or delete entries that turn out wrong. Design changes go
   into `docs/design.md`. No new doc files without a reason.

## Sunday

- 08:00: `uv run arena data` again; the release lands in `data/release-sunday/`.
- 09:00: pre-flight, one practice case through the final machine and setup.
- 11:30: checklist in `docs/submission.md` (key, data, LLM credits, power, no sleep, log file).
- Before 12:00, from `main`: `uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v 2>&1 | tee logs/final.log`,
  then submit that commit hash on ehl.gg.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

"""`buyer` command line: play one case or a whole set with our agent, and pull finished sessions
(result, trace with the supplier's reasons, back office) into logs/ for the learning loop."""

import argparse
import functools
import json
import logging
import os
import statistics
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit import ArenaClient, ArenaError, RemoteTable, play, play_all
from arena_kit.cli import load_env, summary
from arena_kit.play import hosted, play_waves

from . import llm, runner
from .agent import AGENTS, load_package, naive_factory

LOGS = Path("logs/sessions")


def pull(client, set_):
    """Save every ended session of a set that has its trace to logs/sessions/<set>/, once."""
    out = LOGS / set_
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    saved = 0
    for s in client.sessions(set_):
        path = out / f"{s['case_id'].split(':')[-1]}_{s['session_id']}.json"
        if s["status"] != "ended" or path.exists():
            continue
        state = client.session(s["session_id"])
        if not (state.get("result") or {}).get("trace"):  # final: the trace comes after the final
            continue
        try:
            state["backoffice"] = client.backoffice(s["session_id"])
        except ArenaError:
            state["backoffice"] = None
        path.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        saved += 1
    print(f"{saved} new sessions in {out}")


def main(argv=None):
    load_env()
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="buyer")
    ap.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true")
    verbose = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)  # -v also after the command
    verbose.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true", default=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    verbose.add_argument("--no-llm", action="store_true", default=argparse.SUPPRESS, help="template e-mails only")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    sub.add_parser = functools.partial(sub.add_parser, parents=[verbose])
    data = {"default": os.environ.get("ARENA_DATA"), "help": "data package folder"}
    p = sub.add_parser("play", help="play one case")
    p.add_argument("case_id")
    p.add_argument("--agent", default="buyer", choices=AGENTS)
    p.add_argument("--data", **data)
    r = sub.add_parser("run", help="play every playable case of a set in parallel; final: wave by wave")
    r.add_argument("--set", default="practice", choices=["practice", "sandbox", "final"])
    r.add_argument("--agent", default="buyer", choices=AGENTS)
    r.add_argument("--data", **data)
    r.add_argument("--parallel", type=int, default=8, help="cases at once (at most 10)")
    r.add_argument("--waves", type=int, default=5, help="final: stop after this many waves have closed")
    r.add_argument("--cases", help="practice or sandbox: only these cases, e.g. P01,P08")
    s = sub.add_parser("pull", help="save finished sessions with trace and back office to logs/sessions/")
    s.add_argument("--set", default="practice", choices=["practice", "sandbox", "final"])
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    args.no_llm = getattr(args, "no_llm", False)
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.INFO if args.verbose else logging.WARNING,
        format="%(asctime)s %(message)s",
        datefmt="%H:%M:%S",
    )
    client = ArenaClient()

    if args.cmd == "pull":
        return pull(client, args.set)
    naive = args.agent == "naive"
    pkg = None if naive else load_package(args.data)
    complete = None if naive or args.no_llm else llm.complete_from_env()
    if args.cmd == "play":
        table = RemoteTable(client)
        try:
            if naive:
                result = play(table, args.case_id, naive_factory()())
            else:
                result = runner.play_case(table, args.case_id, pkg, complete=complete)
        except ArenaError as e:  # e.g. not hosted, the quota, a paused key: the arena says why
            raise SystemExit(str(e)) from None
        print(json.dumps(summary(result), indent=2))
        state = client.session(table.session_id)
        print(f"replay: {os.environ['ARENA_URL'].rstrip('/')}{state.get('replay_url')}")
        pull(client, state["set"])
    elif args.set == "final":  # no human in the loop: waits for each wave, plays it within its cap
        parallel = min(args.parallel, 10)
        if naive:
            out = play_waves(client, naive_factory(), args.waves, parallel)
        else:
            out = runner.play_waves(client, pkg, args.waves, parallel, complete=complete)
        for case_id, result in out.items():
            print(case_id, result if isinstance(result, Exception) else summary(result))
    else:
        ids = [c["case_id"] for c in hosted(client.cases(args.set))]
        if args.cases:
            ids = [i for i in ids if i.split(":")[-1] in args.cases.split(",")]
        parallel = min(args.parallel, 10)
        if naive:
            out = play_all(lambda: RemoteTable(client), ids, naive_factory(), parallel)
        else:
            out = runner.play_all(client, ids, pkg, parallel, complete=complete)
        for case_id, result in out.items():
            print(case_id, result if isinstance(result, Exception) else summary(result))
        scores = [r["score"] for r in out.values() if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("score") is not None]
        if scores:
            print(f"mean score: {100 * statistics.mean(scores):.1f} over {len(scores)} cases")
        pull(client, args.set)
    if client.practice_remaining is not None:
        print(f"practice sessions left today: {client.practice_remaining}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        state = client.session(s["session_id"])
        if not (state.get("result") or {}).get("trace"):  # final: the trace comes after the final
            continue
        try:
            state["backoffice"] = client.backoffice(s["session_id"])
        except ArenaError:
            state["backoffice"] = None
        path.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        saved += 1
    print(f"{saved} new sessions in {out}")


def main(argv=None):
    load_env()
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="buyer")
    ap.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true")
    verbose = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)  # -v also after the command
    verbose.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true", default=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    verbose.add_argument("--no-llm", action="store_true", default=argparse.SUPPRESS, help="template e-mails only")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    sub.add_parser = functools.partial(sub.add_parser, parents=[verbose])
    data = {"default": os.environ.get("ARENA_DATA"), "help": "data package folder"}
    p = sub.add_parser("play", help="play one case")
    p.add_argument("case_id")
    p.add_argument("--agent", default="buyer", choices=AGENTS)
    p.add_argument("--data", **data)
    r = sub.add_parser("run", help="play every playable case of a set in parallel; final: wave by wave")
    r.add_argument("--set", default="practice", choices=["practice", "sandbox", "final"])
    r.add_argument("--agent", default="buyer", choices=AGENTS)
    r.add_argument("--data", **data)
    r.add_argument("--parallel", type=int, default=8, help="cases at once (at most 10)")
    r.add_argument("--waves", type=int, default=5, help="final: stop after this many waves have closed")
    r.add_argument("--cases", help="practice or sandbox: only these cases, e.g. P01,P08")
    s = sub.add_parser("pull", help="save finished sessions with trace and back office to logs/sessions/")
    s.add_argument("--set", default="practice", choices=["practice", "sandbox", "final"])
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    args.no_llm = getattr(args, "no_llm", False)
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.INFO if args.verbose else logging.WARNING,
        format="%(asctime)s %(message)s",
        datefmt="%H:%M:%S",
    )
    client = ArenaClient()

    if args.cmd == "pull":
        return pull(client, args.set)
    naive = args.agent == "naive"
    pkg = None if naive else load_package(args.data)
    complete = None if naive or args.no_llm else llm.complete_from_env()
    if args.cmd == "play":
        table = RemoteTable(client)
        try:
            if naive:
                result = play(table, args.case_id, naive_factory()())
            else:
                result = runner.play_case(table, args.case_id, pkg, complete=complete)
        except ArenaError as e:  # e.g. not hosted, the quota, a paused key: the arena says why
            raise SystemExit(str(e)) from None
        print(json.dumps(summary(result), indent=2))
        state = client.session(table.session_id)
        print(f"replay: {os.environ['ARENA_URL'].rstrip('/')}{state.get('replay_url')}")
        pull(client, state["set"])
    elif args.set == "final":  # no human in the loop: waits for each wave, plays it within its cap
        parallel = min(args.parallel, 10)
        if naive:
            out = play_waves(client, naive_factory(), args.waves, parallel)
        else:
            out = runner.play_waves(client, pkg, args.waves, parallel, complete=complete)
        for case_id, result in out.items():
            print(case_id, result if isinstance(result, Exception) else summary(result))
    else:
        ids = [c["case_id"] for c in hosted(client.cases(args.set))]
        if args.cases:
            ids = [i for i in ids if i.split(":")[-1] in args.cases.split(",")]
        parallel = min(args.parallel, 10)
        if naive:
            out = play_all(lambda: RemoteTable(client), ids, naive_factory(), parallel)
        else:
            out = runner.play_all(client, ids, pkg, parallel, complete=complete)
        for case_id, result in out.items():
            print(case_id, result if isinstance(result, Exception) else summary(result))
        scores = [r["score"] for r in out.values() if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("score") is not None]
        if scores:
            print(f"mean score: {100 * statistics.mean(scores):.1f} over {len(scores)} cases")
        pull(client, args.set)
    if client.practice_remaining is not None:
        print(f"practice sessions left today: {client.practice_remaining}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

@AGENTS.md
---README
   1 # Codacabana: Tacto Negotiation Arena
   2 
   3 Team Codacabana at the European Hackathon League Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 October 2026,
   4 Tacto track. Our AI buyer for Hollerau Pumpenwerke negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's supplier
   5 bots and closes the deal with the lowest total cost, or walks away. Brief: `docs/challenge.md`.
   6 
   7 ## Setup
   8 
   9 Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).
  10 
  11 ```sh
  12 git config core.hooksPath .githooks   # secret scan, no pushes to main, Entire hooks
  13 uv sync                               # the agent, Tacto's arena kit, pytest, ruff
  14 cp .env.example .env                  # fill in the keys below
  15 uv run arena data                     # data package into data/package
  16 uv run arena me                       # the key works: team and practice quota
  17 ```
  18 
  19 Environment variables (`.env.example`):
  20 
  21 | Variable | What |
  22 |---|---|
  23 | `ARENA_URL` | `https://arena.tacto.ai` |
  24 | `ARENA_API_KEY` | the team key from https://arena.tacto.ai/apply |
  25 | `ARENA_DATA` | `data/package` |
  26 | `LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_API_KEY` | the model, any OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint; optional `LLM_EFFORT` |
  27 
  28 ## Run
  29 
  30 ```sh
  31 uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                     # one sandbox case (free)
  32 uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10     # every hosted practice case (counts against the quota)
  33 uv run buyer pull --set practice                  # finished sessions with trace -> logs/sessions/
  34 uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v     # the Live Final: start before 12:00, leave it running
  35 ```
  36 
  37 ## Approach
  38 
  39 Code owns every number: `buyer/policy.py` plans terms and prices with `total_cost`, cites data
  40 by ID and refuses bad accepts; the model writes one paragraph of each e-mail (`buyer/llm.py`).
  41 `buyer/runner.py` plays the cases. Design in `docs/design.md`, findings in `docs/learnings.md`.
  42 
  43 ## Develop
  44 
  45 Rules for people and coding agents: `AGENTS.md`.
  46 
  47 ```sh
  48 uv run pytest -q                 # our agent end to end against the local arena simulator
  49 uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format .
  50 ```
---DOCSREADME
   1 # docs
   2 
   3 Ours:
   4 
   5 - `learnings.md`: what we know about the arena, its suppliers and the data package, with evidence.
   6 - `design.md`: the agent we are building. `how-it-works.pdf` holds its architecture diagram.
   7 - `negotiation-research.md`: negotiation strategies from the literature, checked against our traces, with an experiment plan.
   8 
   9 Tacto's, copied from [tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit](https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit)
  10 `brief/` at commit `1b5516b` (CC BY 4.0). Upstream is the source of truth.
  11 
  12 - `challenge.md`: the participant brief (story, task, score, rules, timeline)
  13 - `api.md`: the HTTP API, message format, claim checks, the cost function C
  14 - `submission.md`: what to hand in on ehl.gg by Sunday 12:00, and the pitch
---SUB
   1 # Submission and pitch
   2 
   3 What to hand in for the Tacto track, and how the pitch works. Deadline: **Sunday 12:00 on ehl.gg**.
   4 
   5 ## What to submit
   6 
   7 1. **Your repo:** the agent and a README that says how to run it (setup, the environment variables it
   8    needs, without values, and the command). Put the **commit hash** your agent runs in the final into
   9    the description. The jury and tum.ai must be able to open the repo; tum.ai runs a code agent over
  10    every submission.
  11 2. **A short description** of your approach: how your agent prepares, what it reads in the data, how
  12    it decides what to offer, and when it closes or walks away.
  13 3. **Slides** for the pitch. The top 10 present them from 13:00.
  14 
  15 Keep every key out of the repo: no `.env`, no LLM key, no arena key.
  16 
  17 ## At 12:00 your agent is already running
  18 
  19 The code freeze and the Live Final start together, so start your agent before 12:00 and leave it
  20 running:
  21 
  22 ```bash
  23 uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10
  24 ```
  25 
  26 Or your own runner that polls `GET /v1/cases?set=final`. The kit's runner waits for wave 1, plays each
  27 wave's cases in parallel within the 8-minute cap and stops after the fifth wave. From 12:00 there is no
  28 human in the loop, and your agent must not read `/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard` or `/results`.
  29 We check the top 10 for pushes after the freeze.
  30 
  31 Checklist for 11:30:
  32 
  33 - The machine and network you use for the final; one practice case went through it at the 09:00
  34   pre-flight.
  35 - `uv run arena data` ran after 08:00, so the Sunday release sits next to the package.
  36 - `uv run arena me` answers with your team: the key works.
  37 - LLM credits and rate limits for about an hour of parallel play.
  38 - The runner is started and logs to a file; the laptop is on power and does not sleep.
  39 
  40 ## The pitch
  41 
  42 - **The top 10:** the ten teams with the most points after the five waves.
  43 - **5 minutes pitch + 2 minutes of questions**, from 13:00. tum.ai keeps the time; the slot does not
  44   stretch.
  45 - **Every replay is open to the jury.** After the final, each case on https://arena.tacto.ai/results
  46   links to its replay. Pick one negotiation and walk us through it.
  47 - Questions to expect: Why did your agent write that? Would it have worked on a real supplier? What
  48   did your agent learn about suppliers, and from where?
  49 - ⟦Q2: how the Live Final score and the jury combine for places 1-3, and the jury criteria⟧
---PR
   1 ## What
   2 
   3 ## How to test
   4 
   5 ## Screenshot / demo (if UI)
---EXPORTS
   1 # Exports: the Saturday probe sessions as tables
   2 
   3 Every session we played on Saturday 10 October: 15 practice sessions (all 10 hosted cases) and 17
   4 sandbox sessions, joined with the case files and the data package. What we learned from them is
   5 in `docs/learnings.md`. Money is EUR over the case horizon; C is the arena's total cost
   6 (`arena_kit.total_cost`), lower is better. This is a snapshot: the probe and the script that built
   7 it (`buyer/autoprobe.py`, `analysis/export.py`) are in the closed PR #5, commit `03c51bc`.
   8 
   9 | File | One row per | Use it for |
  10 |---|---|---|
  11 | `sessions.csv`, `.jsonl` | session | outcomes: score, C open/deal/alt/best, deal terms, cost breakdown |
  12 | `threads.csv`, `.jsonl` | supplier in a session | supplier profile from the data next to what it did |
  13 | `messages.jsonl` | e-mail, both directions | the full negotiation: terms with C, status, claims, reasons, back office |
  14 | `claims.csv` | data argument we made | which arguments the arena verified, and for whom |
  15 
  16 Join keys: `session_id` (+ `supplier_id`, + `round`). `set` is `practice` or `sandbox`.
  17 
  18 ## How we played
  19 
  20 `method` in `sessions`:
  21 
  22 - `autoprobe v1`: a fixed experiment per supplier thread, then the cheapest valid close. Its steps
  23   are `probe_step` in `messages` and `probe_steps` in `threads`:
  24   - `open`: questions and documents (cost breakdown, delivery schedule or 8D), our anchor price
  25   - `ours`: up to 3 sheets at the supplier's price, each with one lever moved our way
  26   - `theirs`: up to 3 sheets a step below, each with one lever moved its way
  27   - `claims`: up to 3 verified data arguments with a concession
  28   - `step`: concessions until `final_offer` or `agreed`; `push`: one ask after `agreed`
  29   - `keepalive`: a short question so a waiting RFQ thread does not time out
  30 - `scripted probe (resumed by hand)`: an earlier version of the same steps (P01, first P10 run).
  31 - `sandbox A/B: <variant>`: D01 with identical sheets, round 3 varied (`baseline`, `bluff`,
  32   `urgency`).
  33 - `kit naive agent`: the kit's `NaiveAgent`.
  34 
  35 ## sessions
  36 
  37 | Column | Meaning |
  38 |---|---|
  39 | `score` | `(c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)`, clipped 0..1; no deal scores the alternative |
  40 | `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | C of the best opening quote, our deal, our alternative, the best package any supplier would accept (hidden floor, revealed after the session) |
  41 | `gap_to_best_eur` | `c_deal - c_best`: money left on the table |
  42 | `implied_price_at_deal_terms` | the unit price at which our deal's other terms would cost exactly `c_best`; it keeps the deal's coverage, so for an under-covered deal (P08, P18) it mixes coverage and price |
  43 | `deal_*` | the closed terms (unstated fields filled with the supplier's standard terms) |
  44 | `cost_*` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |
  45 
  46 ## threads
  47 
  48 | Column | Meaning |
  49 |---|---|
  50 | `country`, `owner_type`, `credit_index`, `scorecard_colour`, `data_signals` | from the data package (`analysis/explore.py`, `analysis/out/profiles.csv`); signals are persona traits found in notes, letters and news, e.g. `cash_need`, `price_frozen`, `capacity_full` |
  51 | `should_cost` | `should_cost.csv`, the supplier's own plant if modelled |
  52 | `opening_price`, `final_price`, `price_move_pct` | its first and last unit price in the thread |
  53 | `opening_vs_should_cost_pct` | how far its quote sits above (+) or below (-) the should-cost |
  54 | `final_status`, `first_agreed_round` | `open`, `agreed`, `final_offer`, `walked_away`; the round it first said `agreed` |
  55 | `documents`, `sent_cost_breakdown` | attachments it sent |
  56 | `probe_steps` | our experiment sequence (see above) |
  57 | `questions`, `backoffice_calls` | its recurring questions; its internal decisions ("My call: counter / hold / accept") |
  58 
  59 ## messages
  60 
  61 Fields: `round`, `actor` (`buyer` / `supplier`), `probe_step` and `probe_note` (what our message
  62 tested), `action` (`accept` / `walk_away`), `status`, `sheets` (`[{terms, c}]`: our term sheets, or
  63 its standing sheet), `claims_made` (typed as the arena read them), `claim_results`, `missing_fields`,
  64 `signals` (reply delay, validity), `reasons` (the supplier's reasons in words, hidden figures as `…`),
  65 `backoffice` (its roles talking internally that round), `text` (the e-mail).
  66 
  67 ## claims
  68 
  69 `type` (`index_change`, `quality_record`, `delivery_record`, `should_cost`, `volume_change`,
  70 `notice`, ...), `refs` (data IDs), `asserted` (our figure as the arena parsed it), `result`
  71 (`verified`, `contradicted`, `duplicate`, `irrelevant`).

   7 it (`buyer/autoprobe.py`, `analysis/export.py`) are in the closed PR #5, commit `03c51bc`.
   8

  10 |---|---|---|
  11 | `sessions.csv`, `.jsonl` | session | outcomes: score, C open/deal/alt/best, deal terms, cost breakdown |
  12 | `threads.csv`, `.jsonl` | supplier in a session | supplier profile from the data next to what it did |
  13 | `messages.jsonl` | e-mail, both directions | the full negotiation: terms with C, status, claims, reasons, back office |
  14 | `claims.csv` | data argument we made | which arguments the arena verified, and for whom |
  15 
  16 Join keys: `session_id` (+ `supplier_id`, + `round`). `set` is `practice` or `sandbox`.
  17 
  18 ## How we played
  19 
  20 `method` in `sessions`:
  21 
  22 - `autoprobe v1`: a fixed experiment per supplier thread, then the cheapest valid close. Its steps
  23   are `probe_step` in `messages` and `probe_steps` in `threads`:
  24   - `open`: questions and documents (cost breakdown, delivery schedule or 8D), our anchor price
  25   - `ours`: up to 3 sheets at the supplier's price, each with one lever moved our way
  26   - `theirs`: up to 3 sheets a step below, each with one lever moved its way
  27   - `claims`: up to 3 verified data arguments with a concession
  28   - `step`: concessions until `final_offer` or `agreed`; `push`: one ask after `agreed`
  29   - `keepalive`: a short question so a waiting RFQ thread does not time out
  30 - `scripted probe (resumed by hand)`: an earlier version of the same steps (P01, first P10 run).
  31 - `sandbox A/B: <variant>`: D01 with identical sheets, round 3 varied (`baseline`, `bluff`,
  32   `urgency`).
  33 - `kit naive agent`: the kit's `NaiveAgent`.
  34 
  35 ## sessions
  36 
  37 | Column | Meaning |
  38 |---|---|
  39 | `score` | `(c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)`, clipped 0..1; no deal scores the alternative |
  40 | `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | C of the best opening quote, our deal, our alternative, the best package any supplier would accept (hidden floor, revealed after the session) |
  41 | `gap_to_best_eur` | `c_deal - c_best`: money left on the table |
  42 | `implied_price_at_deal_terms` | the unit price at which our deal's other terms would cost exactly `c_best`; it keeps the deal's coverage, so for an under-covered deal (P08, P18) it mixes coverage and price |
  43 | `deal_*` | the closed terms (unstated fields filled with the supplier's standard terms) |
  44 | `cost_*` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |
  45 
  46 ## threads
  47 
  48 | Column | Meaning |
  49 |---|---|
  50 | `country`, `owner_type`, `credit_index`, `scorecard_colour`, `data_signals` | from the data package (`analysis/explore.py`, `analysis/out/profiles.csv`); signals are persona traits found in notes, letters and news, e.g. `cash_need`, `price_frozen`, `capacity_full` |
  51 | `should_cost` | `should_cost.csv`, the supplier's own plant if modelled |
  52 | `opening_price`, `final_price`, `price_move_pct` | its first and last unit price in the thread |
  53 | `opening_vs_should_cost_pct` | how far its quote sits above (+) or below (-) the should-cost |
  54 | `final_status`, `first_agreed_round` | `open`, `agreed`, `final_offer`, `walked_away`; the round it first said `agreed` |
  55 | `documents`, `sent_cost_breakdown` | attachments it sent |
  56 | `probe_steps` | our experiment sequence (see above) |
  57 | `questions`, `backoffice_calls` | its recurring questions; its internal decisions ("My call: counter / hold / accept") |
  58 
  59 ## messages
  60 
  61 Fields: `round`, `actor` (`buyer` / `supplier`), `probe_step` and `probe_note` (what our message
  62 tested), `action` (`accept` / `walk_away`), `status`, `sheets` (`[{terms, c}]`: our term sheets, or
  63 its standing sheet), `claims_made` (typed as the arena read them), `claim_results`, `missing_fields`,
  64 `signals` (reply delay, validity), `reasons` (the supplier's reasons in words, hidden figures as `…`),
  65 `backoffice` (its roles talking internally that round), `text` (the e-mail).
  66 
  67 ## claims
  68 
  69 `type` (`index_change`, `quality_record`, `delivery_record`, `should_cost`, `volume_change`,
  70 `notice`, ...), `refs` (data IDs), `asserted` (our figure as the arena parsed it), `result`
  71 (`verified`, `contradicted`, `duplicate`, `irrelevant`).

1 # Agent design
   2 
   3 The target architecture of our buyer, merged from the team's planning notes (PRs #7 to #10,
   4 10 Oct). What we learned in play is in `learnings.md`; this file says what we build.
   5 
   6 **Status.** The branch `steffen/price-engine` plays a code-only policy with a model-written
   7 paragraph (`buyer/policy.py`, run by `buyer/runner.py`): practice mean of best scores 0.73 (from
   8 0.32), sandbox D01 0.99, D02 0.73. What it does is under "Implemented" below; the rest of this file
   9 is the target design. Julian's draft two (`origin/julian/draft-two`) holds a richer stance and
  10 reader design that is not merged. The architecture diagram is on page 1 of
  11 [how-it-works.pdf](how-it-works.pdf).
  12 
  13 ## Implemented (price engine)
  14 
  15 | Module | Job |
  16 |---|---|
  17 | `buyer/economics.py` | C of a sheet; the accept gate (`deal_cost`); what a sheet is worth to the supplier (`supplier_value` plus overtime for a faster delivery than it quoted); term planning: every allowed combination priced at the supplier's own valuation, lowest C, ties to the supplier's side; the relationship-optimal price |
  18 | `buyer/claims.py` | claim bank: should-cost below its price, our order prices, each cost driver's largest fall over any window up to 12 months, notice period, forecast, scorecard, case rival quotes, hedge and open-book notes; rival offers in an RFQ |
  19 | `buyer/personas.py` | owner type, persona signals from notes, letters, quote remarks and news, cost of money |
  20 | `buyer/policy.py` | per thread: anchor by goal and persona, 30 % of the gap per round, held low after a deep first concession, patience budget for near-cost, fully booked and relationship-goal suppliers; adopts its counter terms when they cost us less, mirrors a better alternative, takes a required index clause; claims 3 in round 1, then 1 per round; close on final offer, agreement or round limit |
  21 | `buyer/reader.py` | the supplier's asks from its fixed sentences (volume, proof, faster payment, our target); no model |
  22 | `buyer/writer.py`, `buyer/llm.py` | the e-mail: a model paragraph that answers the supplier's last e-mail and its asks (no digits, IDs or leaks, else the template), then code sentences with figures (the binding volume), claims and the proposal from code; the forecast rows as a CSV when proof is asked |
  23 | `buyer/runner.py` | one message at a time per session, to the thread whose 60 s clock has run longest; keepalive questions for finished bidders; rollback when a send times out; a guarded move resends our last sheet; the model's time budgeted so every live clock still gets a message; a terminal reply ends the case; accept the cheapest standing sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats the alternative (relationship charge included), after a refused close decide again on what stands; Live Final waves that never raise and resume a crashed case |
  24 
  25 ## Principle
  26 
  27 Code owns every number and every binding decision; the model reads replies and writes e-mails.
  28 Score is total cost C, not price. Every step has a fallback that still sends a move within 60 s.
  29 
  30 ## A case
  31 
  32 1. **Prepare** (before the first move, about 20 s): open the session, build a case brief: C_open,
  33    C_alt, target, walk-away, the lever table (C of each allowed option), a view of each supplier,
  34    and a claim bank of verified arguments. A stance call proposes per-supplier parameters; code
  35    clamps them.
  36 2. **Negotiate**, one thread negotiator per supplier, in parallel. Each round:
  37 
  38    ```
  39    supplier reply
  40      -> READ    (model, hard timeout)  offer, intent, objections, statements
  41      -> CHECK   (code)  supplier statements against the data
  42      -> PLAN    (code)  candidate sheets scored with total_cost, filtered by must_haves_ok
  43      -> DECIDE  (code)  counter / accept / walk away, move size, claims
  44      -> WRITE   (model, hard timeout; template if late)  figures and IDs injected by code
  45      -> GUARD   (code)  every negotiable field, claim format, no leaks, no unplanned figures
  46    ```
  47 
  48 3. **Close**: accept the best sheet that keeps every must-have and beats C_alt, or walk away;
  49    at the latest 90 s before the wave's 8-minute cap.
  50 4. **Learn**: store the trace and what we learned per supplier for the next practice run.
  51 
  52 ## Modules
  53 
  54 | Module | Job | Run by |
  55 |---|---|---|
  56 | Runner | polls the final's case list, one coordinator per case, restarts after a crash | code |
  57 | Coordinator | case brief, starts thread negotiators, shared state, decides when to close | code |
  58 | Economics | C of any sheet, floor, anchor, target, concession steps, accept gate | code |
  59 | Personas | one profile per supplier: traits with evidence, levers, history | model offline, code live |
  60 | Claim bank | arguments as sentences with figure and data ID, computed as the arena checks them | code |
  61 | Reader / writer | supplier e-mail to JSON; move to e-mail | small model, hard timeout |
  62 | Fact check | supplier statements: confirmed, contradicted, selective, unverifiable (not built) | code |
  63 | Guard | blocks leaks, unknown IDs, unplanned figures, broken must-haves | code |
  64 | Fallback cascade | unknown supplier or part: case facts, data search, category averages, its documents | code |
  65 
  66 ## What feeds the brief, by impact
  67 
  68 | # | Data | Decides | Where |
  69 |---|---|---|---|
  70 | 1 | case file, quote PDF | C directly: need, horizon, rates, must-haves, alternative, options, standard terms | `GET /v1/cases`, `arena_kit.docs.standard_terms` |
  71 | 2 | supplier cost floor | anchor, target, relationship charge | `should_cost`, cost-breakdown XLSX on request |
  72 | 3 | index values of its cost drivers | justified price change, strongest claims | `cost_drivers`, `index_values`, `facts.json` |
  73 | 4 | letters, notes, news | what moves it (cash, capacity, relationship), notice periods | `documents`, `correspondence/`, `news` |
  74 | 5 | negotiation history | how far it usually moves | `negotiation_history` |
  75 | 6 | intel, our invoices | archetype, payment lever | `supplier_intel`, `invoices`, `suppliers` (cash discount) |
  76 | 7 | contracts and clauses | notice, index clauses, expiry, single sourcing | `contracts`, `contract_clauses`, `sourcing` |
  77 | 8 | scorecards, QNs | quality lever | `scorecards`, `quality_notifications` |
  78 | 9 | forecasts, PO prices, rival quotes | volume, price history, rival arguments | `forecast_lines`, `po_lines`, `quotes` |
  79 
  80 The Sunday release (`data/release-sunday/`) and the case's own `facts` are read at runtime.
  81 
  82 ## Supplier estimate
  83 
  84 `arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` prices a deal for the supplier from `standard`, `interest_rate`,
  85 `ppm` and `extra`; `relationship_cost` needs `full_cost` and is 0 without it. So we estimate:
  86 
  87 - **Full cost**: cost-breakdown XLSX, else `should_cost` moved by its drivers' index change, else
  88   quote minus an assumed margin. A relationship charge in a practice result reveals the true margin.
  89 - **Cost of money**: cash discounts, cash-need notes, credit index, equity ratio. Seen rates: 0 to
  90   17 %/yr (`learnings.md`).
  91 - **Extra**: overtime for speed (negative) or idle capacity filled by volume (positive), only from
  92   evidence. Volume, contract length and index clauses are not cash in `supplier_value`.
  93 
  94 C_best estimate: the cheapest allowed sheet whose supplier value stays above its floor, or C_alt.
  95 
  96 ## Policy
  97 
  98 A stance per supplier (opening gap, capture, margin, justified share, steps) proposed by the model
  99 at case open, clamped by code to a range per tier and goal, logged with a reason. Fallback
 100 constants when the stance call times out:
 101 
 102 | Constant | Values |
 103 |---|---|
 104 | capture (share of possible saving before accepting) | leverage 0.75, quality_first 0.65, stabilise 0.6, secure_supply 0.55, routine 0.5 |
 105 | opening gap below the quote (never below the floor) | strategic 5 %, important 8 %, standard 12 % |
 106 | margin above full cost for the floor | case's `sustainable_margin_pct` in `stabilise` / `secure_supply`, else strategic 4 %, important 2 %, standard 0 % |
 107 | justified share offered in round 1 of a price increase | strategic 0.5, important 0.25, standard 0 |
 108 | concession steps, only after the supplier moved | 35, 25, 15, 10 % of the remaining gap |
 109 
 110 Live signals adjust within bounds: approval needed shrinks steps (x0.7), high walk risk stops
 111 price pushes. At the target, hold one more round while the supplier still moves.
 112 
 113 ## Build order
 114 
 115 1. Accept and walk-away guard with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`.
 116 2. Term search: every combination of allowed options, scored with standard terms for unstated
 117    fields. Fixes coverage and index-clause losses.
 118 3. Supplier estimate: full cost and cost of money, giving target and walk-away.
 119 4. Claim bank from `facts.json` and the index tables.
 120 5. Persona reading and pacing.
 121 6. Tune on practice traces, one change per batch.
 122 
 123 ## Generalise
 124 
 125 - Branch on features (goal, must-haves, credit, cash signals, owner type, quote content), never on
 126   case or supplier IDs. No constants copied from one case.
 127 - Hold out two or three practice cases for checking only.
 128 - Test failure paths: late model call, malformed reply, a supplier that refuses everything,
 129   missing quote fields, a quote PDF without a standard-terms section.
 130 - Change the agent only for a lesson seen in two cases or clearly general. Freeze early.
 131 
 132 ## Tactics
 133 
 134 Use: data-backed anchors, requests framed as trades, two or three packages to watch the choice,
 135 shrinking concessions with an ask in return, real rival offers cited by ID, a recap of every field
 136 before closing.
 137 
 138 Avoid: invented figures or rival offers (`contradicted`), bluffed urgency or walk-aways (no
 139 effect, `learnings.md`), squeezing a weak supplier in `stabilise` / `secure_supply`, leaking
 140 urgency, budget, target or a missing alternative. Prompt injection of supplier bots counts as an
 141 attack on the arena: never.

1 # Generalisation to the Live Final
   2 
   3 How well the agent on `steffen/price-engine` (commit `9182604`) should carry over to Sunday: new
   4 suppliers, up to a third of cases mixing supplier and case types practice never showed, some
   5 citing the 08:00 release. Research on Saturday 10 October, evening: the kit's code, all 21 case
   6 files, `logs/runs/`, `exports/`, the data package, and our agent on `arena-sim`. No practice
   7 quota spent. Same conventions as `learnings.md`: date, tag, finding, evidence, consequence.
   8 
   9 ## Verdict
  10 
  11 The code runs on every case structure we know. Its tuning is in-sample and unmeasured beyond
  12 the ten hosted cases. The biggest gaps for Sunday: new suppliers get a neutral profile because
  13 the release's letters and news never reach the persona code; one exception loses a whole case
  14 (or every later wave); four or more bidders time out.
  15 
  16 | # | Risk | Damage | Fix | Effort |
  17 |---|---|---|---|---|
  18 | 1 | an exception in a move or the wave poll | a case at its alternative (0 in 6 of 21), or all later waves | catch per move, keep polling | small |
  19 | 2 | release rows invisible to SQL; most suppliers without text | neutral profile for new suppliers | read release rows via the ID index; scan the supplier's e-mails | small to medium |
  20 | 3 | 4 or more bidders | timeouts, lost patience, ended threads | stop sending to the worst bidders after round 1 | medium, a tactics decision |
  21 | 4 | missed phrasings in `SIGNALS` | traits not detected | widen to word stems | small |
  22 | 5 | `price_unit` ignored | wrong-direction rival or order-price claims | divide by `price_unit` | small |
  23 
  24 ## Findings
  25 
  26 ### Robustness
  27 
  28 - 2026-10-10 `rules` **Every known case structure runs end to end.** All 21 public case files,
  29   including the nine never hosted (P06, P09, P12 to P17, P19), played through `arena-sim`
  30   in-process with our agent and the package, no model: no exception, 0 to 1 s per case. Covers
  31   bundles (P07 4 parts, P15 3), the 3-bidder RFQ, `tooling_eur` (P06) and up to 75 term
  32   combinations (P09). The sim's supplier is a fixed script, so this checks code paths, not

"""The model writes one paragraph of each e-mail: it answers the supplier's last e-mail like a
person would (its questions, its points, its situation). Code writes everything that binds or is
checked: figures, data IDs, the proposal. A paragraph with any digit, data ID or leak is dropped
and the template stands in. Hard timeout: the move goes out without the model if it is late."""

import logging
import os
import re
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import httpx

log = logging.getLogger("buyer")
TIMEOUT_S = 15.0
MIN_S = 2.0  # less time than this left on the clocks: the template, no model call
# A late call is abandoned, not interrupted: it finishes in the background (httpx timeout) while
# the move goes out with the template.
POOL = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=32, thread_name_prefix="writer")
FORBIDDEN = re.compile(
    r"\d|\b(?:idx|quote|offer|sc|qn|po|cost|fc|news|doc|ctr):|urgent|urgency|deadline|budget|no alternative|"
    r"walk away|other options|last chance|desperate|must close|time pressure|target price",
    re.I,
)

SYSTEM = """You are a senior buyer at Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a German pump maker, writing to a supplier.
Write ONLY the middle paragraph of our reply e-mail: 2 to 4 sentences, plain text, no greeting, no
sign-off, no lists.

In it:
- answer the supplier's last e-mail like a thoughtful person: respond to what it asked and to the
  reasons it gave, using only the facts listed under WHAT WE CAN SAY;
- acknowledge its situation where the notes give one (for example cash needs, full capacity, rising
  costs, a long relationship), sincerely and briefly;
- if it asks for something we cannot give, say so kindly and point to what we do offer;
- ask one short question only if QUESTION ALLOWED is yes.

Never write any number, price, percentage, date, quantity or data ID (code adds the figures). Never
mention urgency, deadlines, a budget, our alternatives or the lack of them, a target price, or that
we will walk away. Never invent facts, promises or commitments. Be polite, factual and warm unless the
---REPORT
"""What the supplier's e-mail asks of us. The bots write their asks in a few fixed sentences
("Which volume can you commit to?", "Please send us the data.", "Faster payment would help us
more than anything"), so plain patterns read them; no model, no latency."""

import re

ASKS = {
    # a binding volume figure; stated in words with the figure, it was "taken into account" (D01, D02)
    "volume": r"volume (can )?you (can )?commit|binding (higher )?volume|higher (order )?volume|volume figures"
    r"|confirm .{0,40}volume|anticipated (order )?volume",
    # proof of the forecast or of figures we mentioned without an ID
    "proof": r"proof of|send us the data|figures is that based|provide the (volume|forecast|binding)"
    r"|forecast data|volume data",
    # it wants to be paid sooner
    "payment": r"faster payment|pay(ment)? (terms )?(earlier|faster|sooner|within)|need .{0,12}days payment"
    r"|shorter payment|quicker payment|cash flow",
    # it asks for our current price level or our target
    "target": r"what price|which price|your target|price you have in mind",
}


def asks(body):
    """The kinds of ask in a supplier e-mail, in a fixed order."""
    text = body or ""
    return [k for k, pat in ASKS.items() if re.search(pat, text, re.I)]

post-commit
post-rewrite
pre-commit
pre-push

jobs:
  python:

      - run: uv run ruff format --check .
      - run: uv run pytest -q

content.content:
1 # Learnings
   2 
   3 What we know about the arena, its supplier bots and the data package, and what it means for the
   4 agent. Basis, Saturday 10 October: 15 practice sessions covering all 10 hosted cases and 12
   5 suppliers, 17 sandbox sessions, the team's simulator and sandbox experiments, and the data
   6 package. Every euro figure and what-if score below was recomputed with `arena_kit.total_cost`. Evidence: `exports/` (every session, supplier thread,
   7 e-mail and claim; schema in `exports/README.md`) and `analysis/explore.py` (the data package).
   8 
   9 Add findings to the matching section, newest first: date, tag, the finding, its evidence (case,
  10 session or data ID) and what it means for the agent. Tags: `arena` seen in a session, `data` from
  11 the data package, `rules` from `docs/api.md` or the kit's code. Untested ideas go under
  12 Hypotheses. Correct or delete entries that turn out wrong.
  13 
  14 ## Takeaways for the agent
  15 
  16 1. **Stay below the supplier's counter until the end; it agrees the moment our sheet reaches the
  17    counter it would make.** D01: our 51.25 one cent under its 51.30 was agreed at once
  18    (sandbox `14ea35524959126f`). Moving a share of the gap each round keeps it conceding: the
  19    engine took the practice mean of best scores from 0.32 to 0.73.
  20 2. **Verified claims that it "took into account" lower where it stops, most of all in round 1.**
  21    D01 with the same price path: no claims 50.00, delivery record 49.60, notice 49.60, should-cost
  22    49.30, three claims spread over rounds 48.90 (score 0.998). Which types count differs by
  23    supplier (table under Arguments and claims).
  24 3. **Words move it too.** D01, identical sheets, no claims: plain 50.00, "firm" 49.90, warm and
  25    acknowledging its wage costs 49.60, "What would you need from us to move further on the
  26    price?" 49.40 (0.987). But a question repeated every round backfires: practice suppliers
  27    answered "volume!" where volume is fixed and stopped moving (P05, P18 v3). Answer what it
  28    asked; state a fixed volume as our full demand, with the figure.
  29 4. **Patience is a budget of about 40 % cumulative gap** (sum over rounds of our sheet's distance
  30    to its counter, relative to its price): final offers at 41 to 42 % (D01 linear paths), 39 %
  31    (P07), 42 % (P08), 36 % (P18). Suppliers selling near our should-cost or with a pricing
  32    committee end much earlier: Nordmark walked away at 19 % (P02 v1), Ravensteiner gave its final
  33    offer in round 1 at a 15 % gap (P10 v1).
  34 5. **Choose terms by C at the supplier's own valuation**, including a contract beyond our horizon
  35    (free for us, security for it) and the overtime a fully booked supplier charges for faster
  36    delivery (about 0.5 % of the price per day: Hrvelec, Ravensteiner). This alone moved P10 from
  37    a 42-day to a 56-day lead time.
  38 6. **In relationship goals stop at the price where C is lowest.** D01: all claims at once pushed
  39    to 48.50 and scored 0.969; stopping near 48.90 scored 0.998, the relationship charge grows
  40    faster below.
  41 7. **Only a supplier's standing sheet can be accepted** (an alternative returns 422). A better
  42    alternative is sent back as our sheet; it agrees and becomes standing (P10).
  43 8. **Raw-material distributors refuse a fixed price beyond 12 months and refuse any deadband**
  44    (P08, P18): take their clause and negotiate the price; insisting on a deadband stalled them.
  45    But only when their sheet with the clause costs us less than their last one: Nordmark's copper
  46    clause came alone and cost 1.8 % of spend, score 0 (P02 `680eb11405186b42`,
  47    `d52ccdd3d2e07b3f`). That rule separates all 24 P02, P08 and P18 sessions correctly.
  48 9. **RFQ: the arena answers one call per session at a time** and each thread's 60 s clock runs
  49    from its reply, so sends are serialized by deadline; the cheapest rival offer is a new,
  50    verified claim to every other bidder every round (P05 0.83, D02 0.73).
  51 10. **The ceiling is lower than 0.9.** Best per case over all teams averages 0.82 (`/v1/live`,
  52     Saturday evening); practice C_best for P04 needs 4.93 against a frozen 4.94.
  53 
  54 ## Where we stand
  55 
  56 Best score per hosted case, Saturday 22:00: mean 0.776 (team rank 4 of 24 on the practice board;
  57 first place 0.838). Record = best of all teams on `/v1/live` at about 20:30 (house agent in brackets).
  58 
  59 | Case | Goal | Ours | Session | Deal | Record (house) | What limits us |
  60 |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  61 | P01 | stabilise | 0.974 | `4cc256188e1cd8af` | 130.18, Nov, 14 d | 0.995 (0.966) | agreed at our sheet in round 4 |
  62 | P02 | stabilise | 0.735 | `practice-v11-P02.log` | 361.67, 90 d, CU clause 5 % deadband | 0.847 (0.740) | agreed at once at our relationship optimum; the charge (not the price) caps the score |
  63 | P03 | stabilise | 0.923 | `c7fcc4c7ae8f4e9a` | 432.15, 90 d, 24 m | 0.936 (0.925) | price frozen |
  64 | P04 | routine | 0.860 | `81e9fd209c3fd659` | 4.94, 90 d, 36 m | 0.874 (0.860) | C_best needs 4.93 |
  65 | P05 | leverage RFQ | 0.828 | `917135b8156fb8a3` | Dralveck 27.86, 14 d, 35 d | 0.824 (0.555) | ours is the record |
  66 | P07 | routine | 0.751 | `cacd5028b34d30dc` | 5.35, 45 d, 36 m | 0.779 (0.782) | final offer in round 3 |
  67 | P08 | leverage | 0.670 | `practice-v10.log` | 5.26, AS-14404 clause | 0.916 (0.752) | first counter 5.40 with the falling-driver claims; final offer in round 3 to 4 |
  68 | P10 | secure_supply | 0.679 | `7c4f1855794797d6` | 31.50, 56 d, 36 m | 0.702 (0.686) | fully booked, final early |
  69 | P11 | quality_first | 0.710 | `3ac9ee6cf673cf7c` | 45.50, 300 ppm | 0.807 (0.314) | wants faster payment, which is fixed |
  70 | P18 | leverage | 0.621 | `practice-v10.log` | 5.10, AS-14404 clause | 0.677 (0.386) | first counter 5.30 with the falling-driver claims, path 5.20, 5.10 repeats exactly |
  71 
  72 ## Score and terms
  73 
  74 - 2026-10-10 `rules` **The category goal sets the rates of C**, not the case type (P13 is a price
  75   increase under `leverage`, P06 an RFQ under `stabilise`). From all 21 case files:
  76 
  77   | Goal | Fallback risk | Relationship charge | Push for |
  78   |---|---|---|---|
  79   | `leverage` | 3 % (D02: 5 %) | no | price: rival quotes, should-cost, indices |
  80   | `routine` | 5 % | no | price and a quick close; small stakes |
  81   | `quality_first` | 8 % | no | low `ppm_commitment`, chargeback at least `cost_per_defect` |
  82   | `stabilise` | 10 % | yes, sustainable margin 0.5 to 8 % | structure: term, start date, payment, fair clause |
  83   | `secure_supply` | 25 % | yes, 4 to 10 % | full coverage and lead time first, then price |
  84 
  85 - 2026-10-10 `rules` **Every session reveals C_best, also a walk-away**, plus our cost breakdown
  86   computed with the supplier's true numbers, relationship charge included. D01 walk-away after
  87   one message: c_open 448,810.67, c_best 408,623.99. → One session per case gives its target,
  88   and a relationship charge gives the supplier's true margin, i.e. its full cost.
  89 - 2026-10-10 `rules` **Uncovered need** costs `fallback_unit_price` plus `fallback_risk_pct` % of
  90   it; coverage is `min(volume, need) x min(months / 12, horizon)`. Committed volume above the need
  91   is bought anyway; months beyond the horizon neither cost nor earn. Evidence and examples:
  92   takeaway 2.
  93 - 2026-10-10 `rules` **Index clause** cost: `spend x material_share x (|path| - deadband)`, signed
  94   like the case's `index_paths`, plus `index_risk_pct` % of `spend x material_share` whenever a
  95   clause exists. Only a falling path larger than the risk charge makes a clause pay.
  96 - 2026-10-10 `rules` **Late delivery** is `late_cost_per_day x days beyond need_lead_time_days`,
  97   one sum per case. Must-haves can cap the lead time (P05: at most 42 days).
  98 - 2026-10-10 `rules` **Effective date:** units bought before it cost the current price, so a
  99   later start is worth months x volume x price step. Negotiable in D01, P01, P13. D01 at 50.90
 100   and 24 months: April instead of December start, 0.73 to 0.81; plus 60-day payment, 0.87.
 101 - 2026-10-10 `rules` **Our money:** 8 % a year and reference 60 days in all 21 cases. Paying 30
 102   days earlier costs 0.67 % of spend.
 103 - 2026-10-10 `rules` **Relationship charge** (`stabilise`, `secure_supply`) grows with the square
 104   of the first 5 missing margin points, so the cheapest deal sits below the sustainable margin
 105   (D01: about 2 points below its 4 %) unless the supplier's cost floor binds first. It also
 106   moves with payment terms: P02 carried 5,483 at 368.70 and 90 days, 901 at 366.41 and 14 days.
 107 - 2026-10-10 `arena` D01's deal at 50.90 carried no relationship charge, so the foundry's margin
 108   there was at least the sustainable 4 % and its full cost at most about 48.9. Its C_best implies
 109   49.55 (30 days, December start) to 50.13 (60 days, April start).
 110 - 2026-10-10 `rules` In 14 of 21 case files contract length or volume is ours to pick or left to
 111   the supplier's standard terms: D01, D02, P03, P04, P07, P08, P09, P10, P14 to P19.
 112 - 2026-10-10 `rules` No alternative, so walking away scores 0: D01, P05, P06, P10, P14, P17.
 113 
 114 ## Supplier behaviour
 115 
 116 - 2026-10-10 `arena` **The round-1 counter is a cap plus claims, not a reaction to the anchor.**
 117   D01 (quote 52.90), 30 sandbox runs: anchors 44.0 to 48.5 without claims all got 51.30 (-3.0 %);
 118   a should-cost claim alone 51.00, the order prices alone 50.30, notice or scorecard alone 51.30,
 119   all three 50.00; the same three claims at anchor 48.88 got 50.40. An insulting anchor (37.03)
 120   got less (52.30), a shallow one (50.60) 51.40. Words ("what would you need") left the counter at
 121   51.30 and moved the final (49.40 against 50.00). Distributors (P08, P18): anchor 0.787 of the
 122   quote got -8 to -10 % in 13 runs; the same sheets and claims gave 5.43 in one run and 5.57 in
 123   another (supplier-side noise of about 1 %); the order prices and the scorecard "do not change
 124   our calculation", the forecast is "taken into account" without a visible effect. → Open near
 125   0.8 of the quote in leverage cases (deeper buys nothing and costs patience), put the claims
 126   that count into round 1, and treat single-run differences under 2 % as noise.
 127 - 2026-10-10 `arena` **After round 1 each supplier concedes a capped step per round and stops
 128   after a fixed number of counters.** D01: caps of about 1.6 %, 0.8 %, 0.6 %, 0.4 %, 0.2 % in
 129   rounds 2 to 6 (0.8 x our move below the cap), final offer in round 6 at the latest or right
 130   after a move of ours under 0.1 %. Donautal and Werdenfels: 3 counters (r2 +0.04 to +0.20, r3
 131   0 to +0.15), final in round 2 after a +1 % move, in round 3 after 30 % of the gap, in round 4
 132   after three 30 % moves (P08 `f9e9b6dc7ed8e47d`); a move of 55 % of the gap got a hold and a
 133   higher price (P08 `5d30fbf219bdc50a` 5.55 to 5.58, P18 `f038c7d05bfee4d6`). Leitner (P07):
 134   3 counters of 3.5 %, 2.2 %, 1.1 %, final in round 3 in all 5 runs. Nordmark (P02): 4 counters
 135   of 0.93, 0.88, 0.30, 0.07 EUR at a cumulative gap of only 0.03, its reason "as you cannot
 136   commit to a binding higher volume, our flexibility is exhausted". Kalwisz (P11): three steps
 137   of 0.50 then holds at 45.50 "for 300 ppm and 0 chargeback" (it priced 300 ppm at +0.50 over
 138   1500 ppm, `587fe8dcbf9f6c9c`). Ravensteiner (P10): 2 counters. → The round count, not the
 139   gap, ends most threads: make every round count, move 25 to 35 % of the gap, never under 1 %
 140   and never over 50 %.
 141 - 2026-10-10 `rules` **What C_best is made of** (price at which a term combination reaches
 142   C_best, relationship charge 0): P08 5.10 fixed at 90 days, 24 or 36 months (5.06 with the 5 %
 143   deadband clause, about 4.94 with the 0 % clause); P18 4.73 fixed (4.69 at 5 % deadband); P02
 144   368.34 at 90 days without a clause; P11 43.91 with chargeback 500 (43.77 at 300 ppm, 0); P10
 145   28.21 at 23400 units, 24 months, 42 days (27.50 at 56 days); P07 5.03 at 90 days. The records

 440 ## Hypotheses (untested in the arena)
 441 
 442 - Records on P02 (0.85) and P08 (0.73) come from a lower round-1 counter, not from later rounds:
 443   our later rounds converge to the same price whatever the gap (P02 371.9 in v4 to v6).
 444 - Three sheets of equal C for us in round 1 reveal what each lever is worth to the supplier
 445   (payment, lead time, ppm) and could lift P10 and P11.
 446 - The close response of a final case carries `c_best`; calibrating anchors between waves from it
 447   is possible but needs a rules check first.
 448 - Persona-specific wording beyond the generic paragraph (cash need, partnership 2022, reference
 449   customer) moves the round-1 counter.
 450 - Prices fall much further when every sheet stays below the supplier's price and concessions
 451   are slow (house agent 0.75 on P08, ours 0.11 after agreeing in round 2).
 452 - Cash-short suppliers give more price for 14 to 30 days payment than the 0.67 % per 30 days it
 453   costs us.
 454 - Citing the best rival offer moves RFQ bidders; our probe never cited offers.
 455 - Suppliers with "approval above 2 %" notes move at most 2 % per round.
 456 - Stale-costing suppliers concede after a verified falling-index claim; hedged suppliers answer
 457   index claims with "not our reality" until the hedge ends.
 458 - The cost floor is full cost; the five that once sold below full cost may go lower.
 459 - A faster payment package beats a deeper price anchor for cash-short suppliers; test 20 / 30 %
 460   openings against standard / early payment as a 2x2, several runs per credit stratum.
 461 - A `selective` rebuttal (naming the cost driver the supplier left out of its letter) moves more
 462   than a plain index claim.

def supplier_texts(pkg, sid):
    """Every text about this supplier: its letters, call and meeting notes and news, from the
    package and the Sunday release (both reach `ids` and `document`), plus its quote remarks."""
    texts = []
    for ref in pkg.ids("doc:") + pkg.ids("news:"):
        row = pkg.lookup(ref) or {}
        if row.get("supplier") != sid and row.get("supplier_id") != sid:
            continue
        try:
            texts.append(pkg.document(ref))
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - a row without a readable file: its headline still counts
            texts.append(" ".join(str(v) for k, v in row.items() if k in ("title", "headline", "body", "subject")))
    try:
        texts += [r.get("remarks") or "" for r in pkg.query("SELECT remarks FROM quotes WHERE supplier_id = ?", (sid,))]
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - no SQLite
        pass
    return texts


def profile(pkg, sid):
    """{owner_type, country, category, signals, rate, warm}; neutral when the package does not know it."""
    out = {"owner_type": None, "country": None, "category": None, "signals": [], "rate": DEFAULT_RATE, "warm": True}

    try:

    sig = signals_in("\n".join(supplier_texts(pkg, sid)))

def supplier_texts(pkg, sid):
    """Every text about this supplier: its letters, call and meeting notes and news, from the
    package and the Sunday release (both reach `ids` and `document`), plus its quote remarks."""
    texts = []
    for ref in pkg.ids("doc:") + pkg.ids("news:"):
        row = pkg.lookup(ref) or {}
        if row.get("supplier") != sid and row.get("supplier_id") != sid:
            continue
        try:
            texts.append(pkg.document(ref))
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - a row without a readable file: its headline still counts
            texts.append(" ".join(str(v) for k, v in row.items() if k in ("title", "headline", "body", "subject")))
    try:
        texts += [r.get("remarks") or "" for r in pkg.query("SELECT remarks FROM quotes WHERE supplier_id = ?", (sid,))]
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - no SQLite

    return texts

1 # Negotiation strategies: research for our buyer agent
   2 
   3 Research report, 10 October 2026. Two inputs: (1) the literature on automated negotiation,
   4 bargaining, procurement practice and LLM negotiators, gathered by ten parallel research agents;
   5 (2) our own 62 logged practice sessions (`logs/sessions/`), read again to see which of those ideas
   6 fit the arena's supplier bots. Each recommendation says what supports it and how to test it. Most
   7 literature points were read from abstracts and summaries, not full papers: treat effect sizes as
   8 directional (sources and confidence at the end).
   9 
  10 ## Summary
  11 
  12 The current price engine scores a mean of **0.73** over the ten hosted cases (best run per case).
  13 The gaps that remain are concentrated: P10 (0.68, 194k EUR from C_best), P08 (0.55, 79k), P18
  14 (0.49, 37k), P11 (0.71, 28k), P07 (0.75, 23k), P02 (0.51, 23k).
  15 
  16 What the traces show about the bots, in literature terms: a **behaviour-dependent conceder**
  17 (Faratin, Sierra and Jennings' tactic family) that answers each of our steps with a smaller step
  18 of its own, becomes a little more generous late, and ends the dance with `final_offer` once its
  19 patience is used up. It ends the dance after 2 to 6 of our messages, so the 10-message limit
  20 never binds. **The first counter decides most of the deal.**
  21 
  22 Recommendations, ranked by expected gain against cost to build:
  23 
  24 | # | Change | Why | Test |
  25 |---|---|---|---|
  26 | 1 | **Make round 1 count:** three equal-C sheets (MESO), the strongest claims, a precise anchor with a reason | the first counter holds 40 to 100 % of our final price cut; MESOs anchor harder and reveal priorities | sandbox D01/D02, then P07, P08, P18 |
  27 | 2 | **Answer the supplier's stated need every message**, also when the term is fixed | P11 Kalwisz asked for faster payment five times ("you haven't addressed this at all"), then stopped at 45.50 | P11 replay |
  28 | 3 | **Concede in currencies, not price:** hold one or two terms it values back from round 1 and spend one per round as our move | concessions are only answered after a move; logrolling moves price without paying price | sandbox, then P07 / P08 |
  29 | 4 | **Spend patience in fewer, larger steps** | the bot gives back only 0.2 to 0.7 of each step and stops on a cumulative gap; many small steps burn patience without buying price | sweep `FRACTION` 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 on the sandbox (free) |
  30 | 5 | **Expected-value acceptance after `final_offer`** | pushing after `final_offer` walked once (D01); the gain from one more step is small | already behind `BUYER_PUSH_FINAL`; decide from data |
  31 | 6 | **Persona playbook** (table below): the right currency per supplier type | procurement practice and our persona signals agree | per case, one change per batch |
  32 | 7 | **Writing rules for LLM counterparts:** warm, questions, reasons, trades, a story for the boss | largest LLM negotiation study: warmth and questions close deals, dominance causes impasses | wording only; check replies' back office |
  33 
  34 What not to do: extreme anchors (walk-aways roughly triple), threats and dominance, bluffed
  35 urgency or rivals, repeating an unchanged sheet, and anything that targets the bot's prompt
  36 (prompt injection is an attack under the rules).
  37 
  38 ## 1. How the arena's suppliers concede
  39 
  40 From the price paths of every logged thread (script logic: supplier price per reply, our price per
  41 message, statuses). Values for the current engine's practice runs:
  42 
  43 | Case | Supplier type | Anchor below quote | Its first move | Its step per our step (ρ) | Σ gap at `final_offer` | Deal below quote | Score |
  44 |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  45 | P07 | routine, family | 18 to 19 % | 2.6 to 3.5 % | 0.3 to 0.7 | 0.12 to 0.19 | 5.6 to 6.8 % | 0.73 to 0.75 |
  46 | P08 | leverage, distributor | 21 % | 8 to 10 % | 0 to 1.0 | 0.09 to 0.23 | 7.3 to 11.6 % | 0.40 to 0.55 |
  47 | P18 | leverage, distributor | 22 % (7 % once) | 7 to 10 % | 0 to 0.9 | 0.09 to 0.14 | 8.2 to 13.1 % | 0.25 to 0.49 |
  48 | P01 | stabilise, price increase | 9 % | 2.4 to 3.5 % | 0.4 to 0.9, then 2 | 0.08 to 0.10 | 5.2 to 6.0 % | 0.90 to 0.97 |
  49 | P11 | quality first, cash short | 12 % | 0 to 2 % | 0.3 to 0.6, then 0 | 0.15 to 0.18 | 3.2 % | 0.71 |
  50 | P10 | secure supply, fully booked | 7 % | 1.6 % | 0.1 to 0.2 | 0.015 | 1.9 to 2.2 % | 0.67 to 0.68 |
  51 | P02 | stabilise, near cost | 5 % (7 % walked) | -0.7 % | 0.05 to 0.4 | 0.03 | about 0 % | 0.46 to 0.51 |
  52 | P03, P04 | price frozen | 4 % | 0.4 to 1.4 % | 0 | 0.04 to 0.06 | 0.4 to 1.4 % | 0.86 to 0.92 |
  53 
  54 Findings:
  55 
  56 1. **The first counter carries the deal.** In P08 and P18 its first counter already holds 75 to
  57    100 % of the final cut, in P07 and P01 about half. Later rounds add 0 to 4 points of the quote.
  58 2. **It answers our steps at ρ < 1.** If we close the gap fully, the deal lands at
  59    `c1 - ρ / (1 + ρ) * (c1 - anchor)`: with ρ = 0.4 at 71 % of the way from our anchor to its first
  60    counter. Observed: 73 to 90 %, because `final_offer` usually comes before the gap closes.
  61 3. **ρ grows late** (D01: 0.2 early, 1 to 2 in the last rounds), the time-dependent part of the
  62    tactic. `final_offer` cuts this off before we reach it.
  63 4. **`final_offer` arrives early:** after 2 to 6 of our messages, at a cumulative gap of 0.09 to
  64    0.23 of its price (0.015 for the fully booked P10). The round limit never binds. The traces
  65    cannot yet separate a patience budget from a floor that our claims move (the same supplier
  66    stopped at 5.35 to 5.61 in P08 depending on our path, which points to patience).

 163 **Research.** Bayesian learning of the reservation price (Zeng and Sycara 1998), regression on the
 164 opponent's concession curve (Hou 2004), Gaussian-process prediction of its next offers (IAMhaggler,
 165 Williams et al. 2011). With three counters p1, p2, p3 and geometric decay, Aitken's formula gives
 166 the limit: `R = p3 - (p3 - p2)^2 / ((p3 - p2) - (p2 - p1))`. Known failure: when step ratios rise
 167 (slower than geometric) it underestimates the floor and pushes too hard. Every observed counter is
 168 a hard upper bound on the floor.
 169 
 170 **For us.** Useful as a secondary signal, not a stop rule: the bot stops on patience before its
 171 floor, so a floor estimate mostly tells us whether a relationship charge is near (stabilise,
 172 secure supply) and whether a large first concession means room (already `DEEP` in the policy).

 182 payment terms at both sides' cost of money; index clauses with a deadband of 3 to 5 %, a lag,

 184 real; agree chargebacks before the dispute. Preferred-customer research (Schiele et al.): suppliers
